title: Turbocharger/Supercharger Overboost Condition
shortDescription: Boost pressure has exceeded the maximum threshold programmed in the PCM.
fullDescription: The PCM has detected that the turbocharger or supercharger is producing more boost pressure than the system is designed to handle. This is typically caused by a stuck wastegate, a faulty boost control solenoid, or a malfunctioning boost pressure sensor. Driving with overboost can cause severe engine damage including detonation, blown head gaskets, and pistons.
safetyImpact: Engine damage risk; may enter limp mode reducing power abruptly.

causes.cause: Faulty sensor, solenoid, or actuator component
Damaged or corroded wiring or connector
Vacuum/boost leak in turbo plumbing
PCM driver stage failure (rare)

fixSteps.title: Read Freeze Frame Data
fixSteps.instruction: Use an OBD-II scanner with live data to capture freeze frame conditions when the code set, including RPM, load, and boost values.

fixSteps.title: Inspect Boost Plumbing and Connectors
fixSteps.instruction: Check all intercooler hoses, clamps, and the wastegate or VGT actuator linkage for leaks, cracks, or disconnections. Pressure-test the boost system if available.

fixSteps.title: Test Sensor or Solenoid
fixSteps.instruction: Backprobe the suspect sensor or solenoid connector and verify reference voltage, ground, and signal change with a multimeter or scope. Compare to service manual specs.

fixSteps.title: Replace Component and Verify Repair
fixSteps.instruction: Replace the failed sensor, solenoid, or actuator with an OEM-quality part. Clear codes and road test to verify boost behaves as expected under load.

faq.q: Can I drive with a P0234 code?
faq.a: Driving is not recommended. Boost-related faults can quickly cause severe engine damage. Have the vehicle diagnosed before continuing to drive under load.
Only after the underlying fault is repaired and the PCM completes its monitor drive cycle. Clearing with a scanner before repair will likely cause it to return.
It depends on the failed component. Solenoids and sensors are typically inexpensive; full turbocharger replacement can be costly.
